examples.solution_text:
Start at the origin and use the horizontal coordinate first, then the vertical coordinate.

 a. Right $4$, up $3$: $K$.

 b. Right $3$, up $4$: $L$.

 c. Right $2.5$, up $1$: $M$.

 d. Right $1$, up $2.5$: $N$.

For $M$, the horizontal position is halfway between $2$ and $3$. For $N$, the vertical position is halfway between $2$ and $3$.

methods.description: Start at the origin, move horizontally by the first coordinate, then vertically by the second, and mark and label each supplied point. Reversed pairs and multiple points use this same method.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 4/Linear Relationships.md lines 130-190, Plotting Points on a Cartesian Plane and Plot activity a

methods.description: Apply the same movements with a zero coordinate: zero horizontal movement leaves a point on the y-axis, zero vertical movement leaves it on the x-axis, and two zeros give the origin.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 4/Linear Relationships.md lines 122-124 and 160-169; Foundation question 7a-b, lines 320-327

methods.description: Plot horizontal first and vertical second, locating a half unit halfway between consecutive whole-number grid lines.

examples.derivation: Horizontal-first movement places A at (2,5) and B at (5,2). Both solution paths and labelled points match these positions. The method follows source lines 160–190 and image13.
C=(0,3) lies on the y-axis; D=(5,0) lies on the x-axis; O=(0,0) lies at their intersection. The solution diagram matches all three. Source lines 122–124, 160–169 and 320–327 support these cases.

P=(2.5,3.5) lies halfway between x=2 and x=3 and between y=3 and y=4. Q=(4,1.5) lies at x=4, halfway between y=1 and y=2. Both paths and points agree. Source question 9g–j and image30 support half-unit positioning.

Reading horizontal then vertical positions gives a: K=(4,3), b: L=(3,4), c: M=(2.5,1), d: N=(1,2.5). Each match is unique. Source question 8 and image29 support matching; question 9 and image30 support the half-unit adaptation.
